verdict.rationale: ROS 2 provides several bring-up building blocks in its own docs: a launch system for coordinating nodes, parameters for configuration, CLI tools such as `ros2 topic pub` to command a robot, lifecycle nodes and `ros2 doctor`. The project also points to an ecosystem 'from drivers to state-of-the-art algorithms'. Community users agree on parts of this, saying a large existing driver/node base and free teleop and sim take you 'from nothing to something faster than anything'. Others report setup friction: disorganized tutorials with weird errors, too many config formats, and heavy boilerplate. missing for 10: a documented end-to-end hardware bring-up workflow (e.g. a hardware-interface/controller framework), evidence that bring-up actually takes hours rather than weeks, and evidence of reliable first-motion control on real hardware.
